Other times the volume is so low that i turn it up and about 10 minutes, it blasts.  It's just unstable volume control.  It's easy enough to set the alarm and the time.  I like being able to control the display light to make it brighter or dimmer.  Timex is quality for a reasonable price so I am surprised that this alarm does not meet their or my standards.  The radio stations are full of static or some I can't even get although my other radios I have no problem getting the stations on them.  If you just want a standard alarm with a large display, this is good. Canon Powershot S2 IS 5MP Digital Camera with 12x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (OLD MODEL) PROS: Very good camera for most intermediate to advanced users. I have owned this now for almost a year. Great res with the high optical zoom and image stabilizer works well in most situations. This camera takes quite good video for a still camera, and offers an excellent choice for those wanting a still camera and video unit with a budget for only one; just get a large (1GB min, 2 or 4 recommended) high-speed SD card. Like all cameras, batteries get used quickly, get rechargeable Nimh's if you don't already have some, keep fresh in it and another charged set ready to go. Excellent creative tools and auto functions, good manual features as well. LCD screen pivots and tilts for getting overhead shots in crowds, etc.

CONS: Wimpy SD card (32mb) from Canon included. Some noise and blurring in lower light conditions. Standard lens filters need an extender adapter kit from Canon and are too expensive and bulky, so I don't like having my lens unprotected without a UV filter, and wish it had Polarizer. LCD screen is way to small.

I think the newer S3 has better improvements and is probably the one to buy now.

Actual physical doorbell rings only show up in the timeline 50% of the time, often *hours* later.

Sabrent Wi-Fi Range Extender 300mbps 2.4GHZ 801.11N Multifunction Mini Router / Repeater / Access Point / Client / Bridge - Wall Plug Version (WR-WN300) This is a very effective solution to the problem of WiFi dead zones in my house. While signal strength from my Linksys router is good in most rooms, there’s a few areas (such as the basement) where the signal is so weak that maintaining a connection fast enough to stream movies is problematic (spend lots of time looking at the “buffering” message from Netflix). Using this as a repeater has solved that problem.

It’s very compact – the whole router plugs right into the wall and is about the same size as a typical USB charger or similar device. The indicator lights for network connectivity and data transfer are on the front, but are dim enough that they don’t cause a problem at night.

The only notable negative is that the instructions are spotty at best. Getting this up and running is not a problem if you have experience in router setup, but could be tough if you’ve never done it before.

Although I'm using this only as a repeater, it offers additional functionality. It can be used in router mode so it functions as a router, or WISP mode, where it rebroadcasts a wireless network under a different name. I can't speak to how it works in modes other than repeater, but given it's excellent repeater functionality, I would imagine other modes work just as well.

With the exception of the instructions, zero problems with this. It’s a very effective (and compact) solution to extending WiFi coverage. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Sabrent Wi-Fi Range Extender 300mbps 2.4GHZ 801.11N Multifunction Mini Router / Repeater / Access Point / Client / Bridge - Wall Plug Version (WR-WN300)

It is portable enough to lug over to your buddy's house for play dates, but it is too bulky and heavy to carry to work everyday. Construction is very good with an aggressive-looking aluminum case to match the aggressive-sounding "Legion" product name. Mechanical keyboard has decent (but not the best) travel and the large keys are backlit so you can easily play your games in the dark. Dolby Atmos audio works well for games, but is kind of thin for music or movies unless you hook it up to external speakers. This Y720 version has a 1080p IPS display, which is OK but not as bright or contrasty as some other laptops I have used. There is also a more expensive 4K display available, but I have not tried that.

Core i7 CPU with 16GB of RAm gives you really great performance. This machine is easily powerful enough for any games I tried on it. Even though performance is throttled somewhat when run off the battery, battery life is still less than 2 hours under heavy use (maybe 6 hours with light use).

For the money, it is hard to go wrong with these Lenovo Legions. If you don't want to spend more than $1000, the cheaper Legion Y520 is almost as good for most types of games and costs $300 less.

text_fidelity_a:
adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - Night Grey, 2.8 x 5.6 x 7.5 Inches I wear headphones when I work outside, spring through fall. By the end of fall, that year’s pair is pretty nasty from hours of daily use and me sweating in them. Of course I clean them, but it’s impossible to *really* deep clean headphones.

So that’s what drew me to the adidas RPT-01 Sport Headphones: the description advertises “removable, washable knitted ear cushions.” Knit covers I can wash? Hooray!

But there’s no instructions in the box on how to remove the ear covers or the headband. It turns out the cushions aren’t as removable as advertised.The ear cups twist off the headphones (a gentle, counter-clockwise turn), but there’s still an inner plastic rim. I thought I’d be able to wash the knitted cover itself, but nope. And I nearly tore the cover trying to figure out how to remove it, until I found the manual online.

I can’t figure out how to get the headband all the way off. The black plastic lining is removable, allowing the headband to be pushed up. I worry the headband will tear quickly, as the holes that line up with the black plastic lining aren’t reinforced.

Sound quality is okay … as long as I don’t use the Control Knob.

The Control Knob is like a volume rocker and skip/go back button in one. But when I used it to change the volume and skip tracks, I had static that lasted for several seconds.

There is an adidas Headphones app, but I thought it was useless. The only advantage of the app is that it allows you to set up to 3 customizable actions for the other button on the headphones. Oddly enough, at the time of writing this review, the app was only available on Android. I wanted to test the headphones on an iPhone too, but could not because the adidas Headphones app wasn’t available in my country (USA).

Lastly, the headphones are so uncomfortable to wear that I can’t wear them for more than 10 minutes. If I were inclined to use them, which I’m not, mainly because of the static whenever I use the Control Knob. I have a small head, but these headphones are tight and squeeze my ears and head. The ear cushions are actually quite scratchy too.
text_fidelity_b: adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - Night Grey, 2.8 x 5.6 x 7.5 Inches

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons I’m not a hardcore gamer anymore, so for the past few years, I’ve been using a Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball (thumb trackball). I like trackballs for everyday use, and it’s adequate for casual World of Warcraft playing. Most of the time I just futz around leveling alts or doing 5 mans with friends.

But lately I’ve been wanting a mouse I can customize, with more options to adjust my playstyle. It’s cold in my house in the winter, so I wanted to set up mouseover macros and use more mouse buttons, because my hands are cold sitting on the keyboard. So the G502 Proteus Spectrum seemed like a good mouse to review.

I just had one problem: my computer can’t customize the mouse. Why? I have a Mac Book Air.

Now, I know the G502 says on the box that it supports Windows. There’s no mention of Mac support. But I’ve never had a problem with my Mac recognizing Logitech mice, so I figured I’d be safe. What I didn’t know is that Logitech gaming mice have separate software from the Logitech Control Center for regular Logitech mice.

After some Googling, I found the Logitech Gaming Software, which supports Mac OS X 10.8.x and up. I installed it on a Mavericks machine and a Yosemite machine. Neither computer’s Logitech Gaming Software was able to find the mouse. The G502 Proteus CORE is supported, but not the G502 Proteus SPECTRUM.

So right now, I’m unable to customize any of the extra buttons or RGB lighting or any of the other special features. It’s a really fancy basic mouse. I will continue to check for Proteus Spectrum support in the Mac Logitech Gaming Center, and update this review when I can customize things. I’m going into so much detail on the Mac side of things because I know I’m not the only Mac person who tried to use this mouse. I think there’s a workaround with Bootcamp or using a Windows computer, but I’m unable to try that.

I did use the mouse for a few weeks, to test the comfort. I’m really picky on how mice feel in my hand. I’m female and have smaller hands. I like how this mouse didn’t feel too short, and it wasn’t too heavy or wide for me to use comfortably for hours at a time. I also liked the included weights, so you can adjust the weight of the mouse. I haven’t had a mouse with an adjustable weight before, and I liked that extra level of customization.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons

text_fidelity_a:
Dell Inspiron i5547-5780sLV 15.6-Inch Laptop OK, I’ll preface this by saying that while I have used Windows machines, I prefer Macs. So get that out of the way early. As for this particular laptop:
1) it felt a tad unresponsive to me, not horribly so, but noticeably so, at least in comparison to my 2-yr-old Macbook Pro. Certainly faster than my other, older laptop (5 yrs old), but still things seemed to lag a bit disappointingly
2) It’s nicely thin, you can see the dimensions and weight. It feels a bit heavy to me in terms of true portability, especially for having plastic parts
3) I wish it felt more sturdy. The top is strong, and the hinge feels nicely solid and durable. But the bottom and keyboard sections--the black plastic parts-- feel cheap. And I’m not a fan of the slightly rough texture on the trackpad. Keyboard is a nice full size. I prefer a very sensitive, speedy trackpad, so default settings were slow for me, but easy to change. I also find the glare from the black border a bit distracting at times.
4) Wi-fi and Bluetooth set up were easy and quick whether pairing devices or connecting to my network. No problems at all.
5) This isn't a review of Windows 8, so I'll leave that alone save to say I'm not a fan. If you are, this is it.
6) The touch screen is responsive and pretty accurate, though for the life of me I can't figure out who is looking for a touch screen on a laptop. Obviously, some people must like it, but I can't imagine using it hardly at all due to the horrible ergonomics of it. If you're looking for a touchscreen laptop, this seems more than sufficiently responsive and accurate.

It's always hard to compare cross platform. Given a choice between this brand new one and my two-year-old Mac, I wouldn't even consider switching. If I can imagine just starting out neutral--probably impossible to do--I think I'd find it a mid-range product: a little noticeably slow in some respects, a tad heavy but not deal-breakingly so, some sense of durability in the aluminum and hinge but feeling a bit cheap in the other parts, decent screen and sound, very quick and easy plug-and-play-and-connect set-up, a "bonus" touchscreen that I probably wouldn't use at al.

text_fidelity_a:
Schlage WCE100 Home Indoor Camera with Nexia Home Intelligence, White This is the best overview of the components I've seen so far:

Nexia Home Bridge (this is the key component)
Schlage touch screen deadbolt w alarm
Schlage home keypad lock
Schlage home dimmer/appliance module
Schlage home indoor camera
Schlage home outdoor camera
Trane home energy management thermostat
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) remote thermostat
Trane ComfortLink ((tm)) II Control
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) Platinum ZV control (?)
Schlage home door/window sensor
Schlage home motion sensor
Other Z-Wave sensor
Other Z-Wave thermostat
Other Z-Wave lighting device
Other Z-Wave wall switch and outlet

They might have considered making the 9V battery compartment in the "Bridge" just a little bit bigger. It's a mighty snug fit and you have to remove the battery to get the MAC ID. In fact, you have to remove the 9V battery so often it's a curiosity why the battery door is such a pain to remove and why the battery is so difficult to get out of its little bay. I was actually using a flat screwdriver to pry the battery out, it's that tight.

---

Overall, now that the camera, light dimmer and lock and installed, "enrolled" and apparently functional..? WHAT A GREAT SYSTEM!!! The components look great, they're top-quality. Now that I see everything in action (especially video of my home on my iPhone) the subscription fee seems like not such a high price to pay for what you're getting. I know that I'm going to be sorely tempted to add more cameras.

The deadbolt operates with a passcode OR with a physical key. At first I was thinking that you could lock yourself out accidentally but after examining the lock and playing with the buttons I see that is not the case.

I also understand why the light dimmer module goes so well with the indoor camera -- when it gets dark, you'd want to be able to ramp up the light enough for the camera to see! It's a temptation to put the indoor camera in one of my kids room, which is what I might have done when they were small. That would be a rude intrusion these days. So it's outside a hallway that all traffic must pass through. The field of vision nearly covers the two main doors into and out of our home, also. So I can keep an eye on who's getting home when and all that parent-of-teenagers type stuff.

Is there a controller for exterior lights? Or some kind of interface that would allow me to remotely control wired exterior lights?

The only downside to this system, aside from the kludge-y installation process, is that you will want to add more components, and they aren't cheap.

Bottom line: top-quality components, frustrating "enrollment" process -- once you get it all up and running, it's quite impressive. It's nearly worth the frustration to see it all in operation. It would be nice if you could pan-and-zoom the camera. Perhaps that will be forthcoming in another camera model.

I can't help but feel that the process of "enrolling" the components couldn't be made more simple or more streamlined.

Now to budget for an exterior camera... maybe two...

---

Now that I've seen the system in operation I grasp what the manufacturer is actually offering -- remote control of your home administered via your iPhone or iPad. Ideal for working professionals. Getting everything connected and communicating was a little effort, but it's really a beautiful system in operation. You will definitely want to add more light controls and cameras, at least I would. I wonder if there's an exterior light module? There must be. Once you see it in operation the subscription will not be an issue. You are getting more than what you're paying for.

An excellent upgrade to your home and a clever way to keep tabs on a vacation home.
text_fidelity_b: Schlage WCE100 Home Indoor Camera with Nexia Home Intelligence, White

CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact I have two of the larger Cyberpower UPS for my desktop systems and they have performed perfectly for the past (nearly) five years. So, when I needed a UPS for my cable modem and router I picked another Cyberpower. Since the draw on the two attached devices is so low I went with a lower capacity. They have other models that have about the same power output, but this model offers a screen to check load, run time, and other metrics while the unit is running. I've found that screen very helpful on my other UPS' so I went with this model.

Construction quality is very solid. There are 8 outlets - 4 for surge only (and are always on); 4 with surge and battery backup. The battery is replaceable, but I don't expect to have to do that anytime soon - both my other systems are running on their original batteries and still maintain a full charge after nearly 5 years of use.

My cable modem (a Motorola) and router (a Linksys) get about 60 minutes of run time off of the battery, which is more than enough for my needs.

I did not use the included software since I don't have a PC attached, so I can't comment on its features.

Highly recommend for a mid-level UPS system.

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra SPORT Bluetooth Stereo Headset - Black/Yellow (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I am disappointed with these headphones for only one reason: My ears are small, and because of that, these headphones will not snuggly "hang" over my ears like they should. (Children would have the same problem, I expect.) If the over-ear part of the headphones were a little more moldable, I might be able to make them work for me; the extra ear gels themselves are helpful in getting a good fit into the ear canal, but that doesn't keep them from falling off of me. This is why I'm knocking of a star but, again, the problem is not with the headset but with my own anatomy!

With that caveat aside, I love them! For a gardener who wants to listen to something outside while working, the FM radio works just fine and the yellow rubbery cord keeps them around your neck even if you do knock them off. The U.S. Military-grade protection features (against dust, moisture, and shock) make these headphones stand out from the pack.

The Bluetooth pairing and sustained connection with these is better than any other Bluetooth device I've ever used, although I tend not to use Bluetooth unless I'm up and about in the house doing chores. I also don't make or get a lot of phone calls, so we don't even have a cellphone account and depend on the occasional VoIP to get the job done. Meaning I haven't tested the headset features at all.

But the sound is crisp and clear, without mud, more like monitoring headphones used in the music industry. I feel no pressure when wearing them (holding them to my head with my hands, of course, to keep them from falling off of my teensy ears), and I know they would be very comfortable for me in daily use. Maybe I can come up with something to rig them with so they don't fall off. Because I really do like them.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra SPORT Bluetooth Stereo Headset - Black/Yellow (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
ARRIS SURFboard SB6141 8x4 DOCSIS 3.0 Cable Modem - Retail Packaging- White Update Jan 2016: After only a few months of use, the modem started acting up. At first, a reboot would cure the problem, but it got progressively worse whereas I needed to reboot it every few hours. It then failed to work at all even though all the indicator lights were indicating it was functioning properly. Swapped it with a different modem and all the problems went away.

Normally I would not down rate an item because of a failure since everything can break. However, if you expect to get warranty support for this, forget it. Arris/Motorola will not stand behind their product at all.

If you're OK with this being disposable when it breaks, go for it. It did work well when it was working. But, if you expect to get warranty support/repair/replacement, go for another brand.

Original review:
So far this has been a champ in terms of performance. I'm using it with Cox, and it replaces another DOCSIS 3.0 modem I had been using for the past four years (a Motorola SB6120). I got it mainly because I was concerned that my old modem would eventually die on me, and wanted to have a backup.

Installation was simple (just a quick call to Cox to give them the MAC id and serial number). Connection speeds have been slightly better than the SB6120 and more consistent. This seems to run no warmer than the SB6120, which is to say it's pretty warm but not hot when operating. The indicator lights are brighter on this model which, for me, is not a problem given where I have the modem located, but could be an issue if you have your modem out in the open -- the lights are beacon-bright in a dark room.

I'm hoping to get the same solid, dependable performance out of this that my SB6120 gave me. I'll update the review should reliability prove to be a problem down the road. But, at present, this is performing perfectly.
text_fidelity_b: ARRIS SURFboard SB6141 8x4 DOCSIS 3.0 Cable Modem - Retail Packaging- White

Two things that I don't love: One is that the sliding mechanism that opens out to allow you to put the cords in and use the diagonally-sliding plugs easily - they are a little stiff. The other thing is that there is no method for hanging this outlet on the wall. So I have to set it on a high shelf, which is less cool than just hanging it behind my printer or something.

Otherwise, I love that I can neaten up a decidedly un-neat portion of my office with this, and be assured of clean power to boot.

text_fidelity_a:
EVOO 14.1” Ultra Thin Laptop FHD, 32GB Storage, 4GB Memory, Micro HDMI, Front Camera, Windows 10 Home I honestly can’t think of an intended user for this laptop. It’s so sluggish that if I gave it to a kid, I can’t imagine them having the patience to wait for the *browser* to open. Let alone go to a website.

I’m a semi-patient adult in my 30s and wanted to chuck this laptop against the wall because the initial setup took so long. For an example, I tried to load the system information to find hardware information, and it took SEVEN seconds to open the Start Menu and load System Information.

The processor is an Intel(R) Celeron(R) CPU N3350 @ 1.10GHz. The laptop has 4GBs of RAM.

My three-year-old phone has 4GB of RAM and is snappier than the EVOO laptop. I have a Chromebook (Acer R11) that is also about three years old, and it’s snappier, too.

Windows 10 S is the default on the laptop, which doesn’t allow you to install any programs not from the Microsoft app store. I suppose that’s useful for basic users, but if you want to put another browser on, you have to disable S mode. Once you disable S mode, you can’t go back to it.

I thought I’d use this laptop for writing, since it’s so slow to load anything that I wouldn’t be tempted to go online. But I don’t even like typing on it; the keyboard feels like I’m typing on a cardboard box. There’s a hollow plastic sound when I type; it’s *that* flimsy. There are some keyboard shortcuts, but I thought it was odd that there wasn’t a shortcut to adjust the brightness. Considering how long it takes the Start Menu to load, that doesn’t make it easy to change the brightness of the screen.

The trackpad is decent, probably the best part of the laptop for me. It has a slightly sandy texture. For an inexpensive laptop, the trackpad isn’t bad.

The laptop is made in China.
text_fidelity_b: EVOO 14.1” Ultra Thin Laptop FHD, 32GB Storage, 4GB Memory, Micro HDMI, Front Camera, Windows 10 Home

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation) UPDATE 1/5/14: I'm downgrading my rating of this keyboard to three stars for one main reason: there are very sharp edges on the inside of the two sides of this split keyboard which can cut your wrists if you aren't careful. I put my mouse in between the two sides of the keyboard because that is the best position for it for me to prevent back and arm strain. Unfortunately, every time I use the mouse, my right wrist runs into the sharp edges of the inside of the right side of this split keyboard. To give you an idea how bad this sharpness is, I wear a [[ASIN:B008C27UPQ sport wristband]] to protect my wrist, and it is literally shredding from coming in contact with the knife-sharp plastic edge. I have tried putting duct tape over the sharp edge, but it won't stick to the plastic this keyboard is made of, and to add insult to injury, the tape looks awful.

Previous Review:

I recently had a bad flare-up of right arm pain from repetitive stress. I experimented to figure out which movements at my computer were hurting me the most, and I realized that reaching for the mouse was even more painful than keyboarding. As a result, I searched for keyboards here on Amazon with the potential to be divided in half, so that I could place my mouse right in front of me. That search led me to this keyboard.

This "freestyle" keyboard gives you the option to either leave the two sides hooked together and place it at a 45-degree angle on each side, or unhook the two sides totally. It is a simple procedure, no tools required, to unhook the two sides.

This product comes with instructions for putting the keyboard together from scratch, but everything came assembled except for mounting the padding that supposedly goes under your wrists--I have medium-sized hands, and the padding lands at the base of my hands, nowhere near my wrists. The padding also is not very thick, and I'm not sure why the manufacturer did not just go ahead and paste on the padding themselves--it's a hassle making sure it is totally straight before you stick it on. It can't be re-positioned if you mess up. Fortunately, I didn't mess up, and I don't have a huge need to support my wrists, so I am not downgrading my rating for that, but some consumers might want to know about it.

I really like the ability to put my mouse pad in between the two halves. This works as well as I had hoped to prevent the strain of reaching for the mouse constantly. The keys have a nice feel to them, as well. I am a touch typist, and I was very concerned at first that I would lose that ability on a strange keyboard. I have learned after multiple long days of using the keyboard that the trick is to get my fingers in the right position to begin with, such that my right pointer finger is on the J, and my left pointer finger is on the F. Even so, I currently hit false keys much more than normal. I hope that time and use will overcome this issue. I have ordered an additional one of these keyboards to hook up to my laptop so that I am always employing the same keyboarding reflexes, in order to more quickly retrain my brain.

This keyboard is certainly much more expensive than the $15-19 keyboards I've used forever, but will be well worth the price if it, as I think it will, helps prevent the excruciating pain of repetitive stress syndrome.

This keyboard is made so that the inner section can be elevated at either of two selected heights, or it can be fairly flat. This is useful for varying the position of the hands. As a physical therapist told me years ago, changing position and resting are crucial for preventing repetitive stress. I've tried all three levels, and I find the highest one the most comfortable.

Another plus of this keyboard is that I can now bilaterally employ a beneficial PT suggestion: I have for years placed a pillow under my right arm which is positioned against the arm of my [[ASIN:B000PWGZOI rolling office chair]]. This takes the strain off my arm and shoulder by bracing them. The fact that I'm using a pillow means that I am not in danger of damaging the brachial plexus nerve in the axilla (underarm), which can happen with hard objects like crutches. Previously, it never felt comfortable when I used a traditional keyboard to do this for my left arm, but with this keyboard, it does. Now, with both arms/shoulders braced, I find that it is much easier and even automatic to keep my back straight and my head up. It has greatly eased not just arm and hand strain, but back, shoulders and neck strain as well. In addition, I make a point to take my hands completely off the keyboard and mouse when reading, vs. keyboarding, and the pillows give me a comfortable place to elevate my hands, on the top of the pillow where it extends from beneath my underarm.

I rate this product as follows:
Ease of use: 4 stars (should improve with practice)
Functionality for preventing muscle strain: 5 stars
Comfort of use on wrist: 3 stars
Ease of assembly: 4 stars
Attractiveness of keyboard: 4 stars
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 Ergonomic Keyboard w/ VIP3 Lifters for Mac (9" Separation)

ASUS ZenPad 3S 10 9.7" (2048x1536), 4GB RAM, 64GB eMMC, 5MP Front / 8MP Rear Camera, Android 6.0, Tablet, Glacier Silver (Z500M-C1-SL) As a long-time Apple user, I am strongly considering other options because of a number of issues, including software updates that slow to a halt older devices ("planned obsolescence" is what they call it). Between that, the higher cost, and a few other things, I'm in the market for a different tablet and computer.

In the past, the problem switching back was that, unlike with Apple, things were not quite as user friendly with the interface and you had to really figure things out instead of it being immediately apparent.

Happily, it was different with this tablet. Out of the box, my family and I were able to figure it out quickly and easily, giving us hope in another option.

Quality: Great image on the screen with very high resolution! The feel of the device is also sturdy, aesthetically pleasing, lightweight, and thin.

User-friendly layout, very accessible, good features, and it works seamlessly with Google. I've got google email and YouTube channels, so it's nice to know there's a trade-off for losing some of the other things like seamless transitions between iTunes, my current calendar (not in love with that--I can just as easily switch to google or droid for this)...

All this adds up to the following: Apple can no longer claim to be the clear leader in tablets, phones, and computers. They have stopped innovating far beyond comparable products, and now, for the value and overall performance, the ZenPad is a worthy adversary.

I still have my MacBook Pro computer, but when it comes time to buy a new one, I will be ready to switch knowing items like these are available.
What a great surprise!
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ZenPad 3S 10 9.7" (2048x1536), 4GB RAM, 64GB eMMC, 5MP Front / 8MP Rear Camera, Android 6.0, Tablet, Glacier Silver (Z500M-C1-SL)

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Leather Case, Onyx Black - fits all Paperwhite generations prior to 2018 (Will not fit All-new Paperwhite 10th generation) After being a NOOK user for just over a year, I fell in love with the Kindle Paperwhite, decided to switch platforms, and joined the Kindle family in February. After using the Kindle for about a week without a cover, I felt I needed to protect my new device. I bought two cases from third party vendors, and they were just okay. My Paperwhite seemed to float around inside these cases, so I bit the bullet and bought Amazon's leather cover in Fuchsia. When I received it, I wasn't thrilled with the color, so I returned it and got Onyx Black instead. While I love it--it's very stylish, elegant, and the border blends perfectly with the device--my Kindle also kept blending in with other tech gadgets around the house that live in black cases. I went to Best Buy and looked at the case in Royal Purple (in my area, they only sell Onyx Black, Fuchsia, and Royal Purple), but again I didn't care for that color either. On a whim, I ordered the Persimmon case, which I got yesterday. I'm very happy!!! It is a beautiful coral color, not what the Amazon website depicts, but also not a true red, and the trim accentuates the Kindle perfectly. I don't find it distracting. I have been so happy with this case that I paid the extra $20 to turn off Special Offers and it works as advertised. The Kindle sits perfectly flush inside, closes flush, and even when I fold the front cover back there's no floating (very distracting when you're reading and the Kindle "shifts" when you move your finger to turn a page). Anyway, I'll be selling the Onyx Black case, which is, after one month of use, in excellent condition. I highly, highly recommend these cases for the Kindle Paperwhite, and if you like cheerful, bright colors, go with Persimmon. The only cons I can think of are: there should have been a teal and green option, and I wish the inside of the front cover had the Kindle logo engraved on it (don't think that's a lot to ask for the price; instead the inside logo feels like it was ironed on).
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite Leather Case, Onyx Black - fits all Paperwhite generations prior to 2018 (Will not fit All-new Paperwhite 10th generation)

CozyPhones Sleep Headphones - Over Ear Headphones from Ultra Thin Cool Mesh Wired for Side Sleepers, Meditation, Running, Laptop, and Phone - Pink Lycra This sleep headphone band fits quite comfortably. Before I bought this I was introduced to the product at my mom's house and I wear a considerably bigger hat size than her, but the stretchy band fit both of us perfectly. Despite my big bobblehead of a noggin, I don't find this too tight even when worn for hours, and yet it hasn't become stretched out either. A smaller headed person could still wear mine. Also in regard to fit, the light weight, low profile speakers can easily be moved inside the headband to exactly where they are most comfortable and best heard for each wearer (I did have to move the speakers back when I tried my mom's). Once in place the speakers stay put really well simply due to the friction between the textures of the fuzzy fabric pad over each speaker and the headband's fabric. I occasionally have to tweak where a speaker is sitting as I put them on, but once in place the speaker has never needed to be repositioned during wear. I also love that the speakers can be slipped out through the back so the headband can be laundered.

I would say that the sound quality is that of average headphones. I don't notice a discernable difference between these and any other headphones I own, but I may not have as attuned an ear as some people seem to have, so my feelings won't be hurt if you get a second opinion on this part.

I don't really have any cons to mention for these, but wait, I almost forgot to mention that when buying these I saw multiple other reviewers warn that the dye bled from the colored edge of their headbands. I should say that I specifically bought the one with the white edge to avoid that happening. I've had no dye transfer at all from mine, so I can suggest getting the white edged band if that's a concern.

Hope this helps.

- EASY setup. The time it takes to send an eMail and receive a reply, and a few seconds more. I have heard people say it requires iPhone 4 and up - I have a 5 and everything was a breeze. I didn't use the picture feature initially but it was no problem to update later.

- Decent map feature - good enough to get you in general range of the FIND radius.

- An audible FIND jingle. Just loud enough to hear through a wallet. Louder sure would be better, but it has a tinny high-pitched jingle that's easy to identify once you've heard it.

- It's small enough to fit in my wallet. It's a bit bulky, but it does.

- It's weatherproof and sealed. I haven't actually tested that and don't want to, but it's a nice feature.

- On-phone settings are easy to operate, and allow you to turn off Bluetooth tracking without turning off the iPhone's Bluetooth.

- Easy to assign to other objects as needed (if you don't use the stick pad.) It has a hole, so you don't HAVE to stick it to anything permanently.

- Can add other users (beforehand, of course!)

- It works. The battery is only supposed to last about a year, though (we'll see!)

Cons:

- Bulkier than I thought - not quite as thick as a pen, but almost. About a half-dollar size.

- The FIND process takes a minute or two to adjust and is a little confusing at first.

- The FIND radius sure isn't perfectly accurate. But hey, it's something!

- Battery not replaceable. The Tile people will recycle it for you for a fee, but I doubt that is a rapid process.

I really like it. I don't lose stuff that often, but this is an awfully convenient tracking option - having a general idea is a LOT better than having NO idea at all! And I LOVE the idea of the Tile community! The Tile gives me peace of mind taking things through airports etc. If there's something you think you MIGHT mislay, I think the Tile is worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Tile - (Gen 1) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer

text_fidelity_a:
JVC Soft Wireless Earbud with Stayfit Tips, Remote and Mic and Bluetooth Violet (HA-FX9BTV) 3.5 stars taking price into account

With headphones, it is always a blend of "you get what you paid for", and comparing to others at a similar price point.
How do these compare? Well, they are about average for the $20-$40 range. Not much better, not much worse. And as is the case with headphones, for a bit more, you can do MUCH better, and for a bit less, you will get roughly similar results. (In other words, headphones under $75-$100 are, more or less very similar, and then suddenly, your options get drastically better.)

Here's my analysis on the general sound quality and other features:

MISC:
Phone calls: 5 stars: Easy to use, works great for calls on both ends, and blocks outside sound quite well!
Ease of use/pairing: 5 stars: It passed the test of not having to read instructions, meaning it is incredibly simple to pair and use
Appearance: 5 stars: Neat! It's colorful and fun, as well as practical and functional!
External noise: 4 stars: Because it has a pretty tight seal, it is like an earplug, blocking outside sound quite effectively
Comfort: 3 stars: comparable to others of this design. Totally fine at first, and annoying after long use.

SOUND:
Treble: 2 stars: quite tinny
Bass: 2 stars: ok depth, not great, not very powerful
Overall: 2 stars: not much detail in the sound, but it can get pretty loud without distorting, and it is definitely good enough for basic listening and phone calls. There also appears to be a *very slight* hiss in quiet/silent moments when the volume is louder.

OVERALL:
The average is 28 out of 40 possible points, or 70% (a "C" grade, if it were going to school ;-), but because the above analysis does not take price point into account, comparing this to brands like Bose, as well as dollar store headphones, this means that for the current list price of roughly $29.99, this is a reasonable expectation.

The average number of stars based on my rubric is 3.5 stars: decent for this price point, and certainly good enough to enjoy music and spoken word, and to have successful phone calls.

Western Digital 3TB WD Purple Surveillance Internal Hard Drive HDD - SATA 6 Gb/s, 64 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD30PURZ I purchased this as a data storage/backup drive for my desktop PC. My main drive is a1TB NVME drive. The data drive I use for movies, songs, and backups and digital images. Since I am not booting with the drive I don't care about raw performance, nor will I pay for it. With that said I am VERY happy with this drive. It only spins at 5400 RPM, so the access time is slightly slower, but it makes no difference to me. Maximum transfer rate is nearly 200MB/sec. High capacity drives have dense platters and are able to pull data faster.

I am a Nazi for eliminating extraneous sound and used to keep my drives inside enclosures to reduce sound. My quietest drive to date is the Samsung HD 503HI, and this is even quieter. I have several large case fans spinning slowly and if I turn them off I can ever so slightly hear a faint humming or click, but otherwise I hear NOTHING.

This is my first WD drive (have always used Samsung). I cannot speak to the drive's reliability as I've only had it for one month. It is labeled for "Surveillance," so if it's meant to be running 24/7- 365 it is meant to get use in commercial/industrial environments.

I think everyone with a desktop PC should adopt this system. It is very easy to backup anything important- save it to your C: drive as well as your backup E: drive or whatever. If one your main drive goes kaput you have the backup to pull your saved data from. You can use flash drives for additional redundancy and portability, but in my experience they are not so reliable.

Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver After an attempt to use [[ASIN:B005INJ4ZG My Zone Wireless Headphones]] was a bust for me due to its terrible sound quality, my techie husband bought this amp for me as part of a setup that allows me to listen to TV as loud as I want without disturbing him or the neighbors.

I directly hook up this amp to a head phone or earbuds when I am sitting close to the TV by using a special [[ASIN:B00009UVPN adapter]]. Head phones and earbuds have a 1/8 inch (3.5 mm) male jack (AKA male connector). Without an adapter, they can't be inserted into this amp, whose plug (AKA socket, female jack, or female connector) measures 1/4 inch (6.35 mm).

Because I like to move around my living room when I am watching TV, my husband also bought me a special [[ASIN:B0010CX798 male-to-female, headphone adapter, extension cable]]. The 1/4-inch, male jack of this cable fits into the 1/4-inch plug of this amp, and it has a 1/8-inch plug on its other end into which the jack of a head phone or ear bud can fit.

In order to use this setup, my husband also hooked into this amp a [[ASIN:B000068O3F male-to-male extension cable]]; one end is 1/8-inch and the other is 1/4-inch in diameter. The smaller end fits into a plug on the TV. When I want to use this external speaker source, I use the TV remote to access a menu that allows me to do that. Once this system is hooked up, I can no longer adjust the sound volume on the TV itself. I use the volume control on this amp.

Note that there is no On/Off switch on this amp. If you want to turn it off, so that you are not wasting electricity when it is not in use, you unhook the power cord from the far-left side of the amp.

This setup is a little complicated for the non-techie to figure out on their own, but if you have anyone techie in your family who can do it for you, it works really well.
text_fidelity_b: Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver

Patriot Memory Supersonic Boost XT USB 3.0 8GB Flash Drive (PEF8GSBUSB) While I do most of my work at the office, there are times that I want, or need, to work on certain things at home. This was the easiest and most cost effective way to be able to transport documents home and back to work again. I ordered this particular flash drive becasue not only did it have a key ring attachment, it also appeared to be pretty rugged and well protected. Many others leave the USB port open/exposed and that just felt a little risky since I knew I would be carrying it back and forth every day. Upon opening it, I liked it! It is not as small and flashy as many others but for my purposes it was perfect. It felt very durable and I wasn't worried about carrying it around with me all the time. I put it on my work key ring and have enjoyed the convenience of having it. I especially like this drive because there is no software to download or set-up required. I just plug it in and go to work.
I loved it until a couple of days ago when I pulled the cap off only to find I had pulled the entire unit out of the protective case. I was worried about the USB being exposed and now the whole flash drive chip was exposed! There is a small clear plastic piece that nests just inside the lip of the rubberized case that keeps the unit in place inside the casing. When I tried to pull the cap off, which is a bit snug, it pulled the entire unit out, dislodging the small plastic piece. I have tried to slide it back into place, but to no avail, so there is no longer anything holding the "guts" of the drive inside the casing. I was not being too rough on it and have intentionally tried to gently remove the cap every time I use it. From such a rugged, solid first appearance, I am very dissapointed that this happened just a little over a month after receiving it, So far, I have still been able to retrieve my data off the device so I have not lost anything there. And luckily I ordered this from Amazon, a company that is fairly easy to work with. They will be providing a replacement so all I am out is the effort to transfer the data over to the new unit. I hope the next one will hold up because I really did like it and I would like to be able to enter another review letting you know that this one was just a fluke. We'll see!
text_fidelity_b: Patriot Memory Supersonic Boost XT USB 3.0 8GB Flash Drive (PEF8GSBUSB)

Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter I wanted to hear and see Skype on our Sony XBR7 HDMI-only capable 1080p TV, fed from a Lenovo X220 convertable laptop/tablet running System 7 64 bit Ultimate through the DisplayPort. I also wanted to watch some YouTube videos playing from Firefox and hear their audio on my big living room audio system. No such luck.

When first plugged in, I remember briefly seeing the TV via this DisplayPort adapter in the audio device list, but the next time, the TV disappeared and is nowhere to be found. Not in the audio control panel, anyway. It's just gone.

I first chalked this up to the Thinkpad weirdness, as its internal audio card/mic doesn't work with Skype either. If I plug in an external Logitech webcam, it works seamlessly. Internal camera/mic, nothing.

Sony audio problems aside, the video looks great on the big screen, though it overscans a bit and cuts off part of the menu bar at the bottom.

One reviewer said he could see his TV in the list of audio devices and was able to configure its audio to satisfaction. My Sony TV does not show in the Lenovo audio devices list, though it does show as a generic PnP monitor.

I plugged the HDMI cable into a tiny 7" video monitor and whatdayaknow, the audio came through and the device showed up as an audio device. Then I plugged it into a 20" Vizio and sure enough, it works fine too. Same with a Samsung LCD. Three monitors out of four work. The Sony is the only one that doesn't. Hmmmm.

Sooooo, I'm guessing there's something about Sony's DRM or some other HDMI protocol blocking the computer from seeing the TV. I set all the TVs for internal speakers. Routing audio to an external amp is another variable in the equation.

Nothing wrong with the adapter that I can tell, it simply doesn't see certain Sony TV's.
text_fidelity_b: Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter

Samsung 970 EVO Plus SSD 2TB NVMe M.2 Internal Solid State Hard Drive, V-NAND Technology, Storage and Memory Expansion for Gaming, Graphics w/ Heat Control, Max Speed, MZ-V7S2T0B/AM Modern computers are a lot more reliable than computers from 10 or 20 years ago. Computers are not getting a lot faster every year like they used to. I no longer replace my computer every couple of years. If your computer is getting a little sluggish, instead of replacing the whole thing, you can usually give it a huge performance boost by upgrading just key components. In particular, upgrade your memory and upgrade your hard drive. This SSD does not add a lot of capacity, but it gives you a lot of speed so that programs or databases that you use a lot will load much more quickly.

This drive installed and formatted easily on my Windows 10 desktop computer. It's been running flawlessly since then and the performance has been blazingly fast.

There are a lot of different SSDs on the market these days. Check your computer manufacturer's website to see what is compatible with your motherboard. This SSD costs 2 to 3 times as much as entry-level products with the same capacity. The more advanced design makes it more than twice as fast as more basic SSDs. If you use your computer for computer-aided design, graphics/video editing, or hard-core gaming, then the speed may be worth the price to you. For general purpose office or home computing, the entry-level SSDs are probably fine for you.

Logitech Squeezebox Boom All-in-One Network Music Player / Wi-Fi Internet Radio (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The Squeezebox is a radio that you can use to play internet radio, radio services such as Sirius, and music from your hard drive from anywhere in the house.

Setup is quick and easy. You simply install the Squeezebox software and then create a Squeezebox account. The squeezebox account takes seconds to setup. Once you set it up you tell it what radio services you have. I have a Pandora and Sirius Internet Radio account. You enter your login info, and after it verifies it you are setup.

If you do not have any of these, the wizzard will set one up for you. It also works with services such as Rhapsody and Live365.

Using the Squeezebox software you then identify where you music files are located and where your playlist information is located and then that is done.

You then turn on your radio. It automatically connects to your WIFI connection in your home. Using either the control knob on the box or the remote control you can choose your radio services. Within 10 minutes of UPS delivering the box I was listening to Sirius, Pandora, and my iTunes music from my upstairs bedroom.

The sound is great. Truly exceptional with full deep bass and clear crisp tenor and high ranges. Even at low volumes the unit sounds great.

The unit also has a sleep timer, clock, and alarm features. There are several presets to set so you can choose favorite songs or stations quickly and easily.

Pros: Easy setup, works with mac or pc. Uses existing services you probably already have. Wonderful sound, small design.

Cons: The only real con I see is that the unit is a little pricy. Also the menus on the unit take a little getting used to as there are many menus and options nested within each other.

Overall this is truly a wonderful product. Great sound, easy setup, and ease of use. Truly great for audiophiles.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Squeezebox Boom All-in-One Network Music Player / Wi-Fi Internet Radio (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
GolfBuddy GB-WT3 Golf GPS/Rangefinder Watch Black To answer the first obvious question, yes, it can be worn comfortably on even fairly thin man's wrists. And it looks surprisingly good for something with these features. It does look like a quality object and - although a little bulky - I don't think it will bother anyone used to wearing men's wristwatches. I'm still trying to decide if the fact that it says "Golf Buddy" on it is silly, but I guess not for someone into golf and showing off their toys.

Unfortunately, you cannot get full layouts of courses with this watch, nor can you study any aspects of the course until you are there. But it does give you some very pertinent information while on the fairway or the green. But this is the tradeoff between this and a big golf GPS - you get a more convenient, less cumbersome, and less likely to annoy your friends because you're pulling it out to play with it when you should be putting device, but without the full color maps, weather and other junk you could replicate on your cell phone. And actually, I think it's a pretty nice compromise - you don't want to get so engrossed in electronics while you're out enjoying nature and weather and sport.

I also really like that it can do some basic watch and pedometer features like stopwatch, sunup/sundown, and show you how fast you are walking/biking/riding. On the flip side, since it already has the GPS, clock, and a bunch of programming script, it seems like it should house a lot more of those features; I almost expected to have many menus to explore and new features to discover for some time, but this was not the case.

It has a crazy charging "station". These days, I prefer anything just have a micro USB port so I don't have to think about extra cables or charging devices, but that would be difficult to incorporate and retain its water resistance, so it's probably the right solution, except since it has a USB-A end anyway, it should come with a 5V rectifier (most - but not everybody - has excess of these lying around).

This is a pretty nifty device for an enthusiast of both golf and gadgets, who doesn't want to bog down the game by looking at their GPS screen all day long.
text_fidelity_b: GolfBuddy GB-WT3 Golf GPS/Rangefinder Watch Black

text_fidelity_a:
Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth) The sound quality on this machine is amazing.

It is kind of hard to set it up. You use a microphone (included) to get the acoustics of the room. This is pretty normal. Then you have to set the sound field to match the source video or audio. That's not so standard. Denon, for example, can automatically detect what the source is putting out and adjust automatically. It took a while to figure out what lined up with what, but once I had it all sorted out, I was a very happy camper.

The range of audio, high to low, is very impressive. The bass is amazing. Naturally your speakers will play a role in this, more so than the receiver will, but with the right speakers this unit is pretty amazing. 7.2 strikes me as odd. There is only one audio channel that goes to the subwoofer, so the same sound is sent to both. Humans can't audiolocate subsonics, so there isn't much surround quality involved.

It supports both WiFi (with a good antenna that sticks up from the back) and Ethernet. As with any device, Ethernet will give you the more reliable connection.

It supports Blutooth, which is kind of cool. I use it to stream Audible books from my Kindle Fire. It's very easy to set up.

It supports passive HDMI, which is really nice. You don't have to have everything turned on if you don't need it. When the system powers itself down, which it does if it is inactive for two long -- say if you leave a video or disk paused -- the screen barely flickers.

It does not yet have support for Sirius, which is disappointing, but it supports other services, such as Pandora and, of course, Sony's own Music Unlimited service.

text_fidelity_a:
Yamaha AVENTAGE RX-A880 7.2-ch 4K Ultra HD AV Receiver with HDR Dolby Vision Dolby Atmos Wi-Fi Phono YPAO and MusicCast. Works with Alexa. Update: I really love this machine. You give a lot of things five stars if they're really good products, but this one deserves bonus. I've been slowly going through the full 200+ page manual to make sure I don't miss any features and to get the most out of this thing, and I'm continually thrilled. Also, I give a lot of things controlled by apps low ratings because I tend to hate screwing around with my phone, but in this case, the Yamaha AV controller app only adds to the value, with the best part being you don't NEED it to take advantage of all the receiver's functionality, but it's a joy to have sometimes to make fine adjustments without having to turn on the TV. I really like it for adjusting net radio stations and stuff like that or fine tuning music sounds - again, without having to turn on the TV. This also makes up for the one negative I mentioned below about not being able to change all the settings from a web page. Great stuff!

Original review:

Before this, I had two Sony receivers in my living room. My secondary is a much older model - about 12 or so years old - that does not have HDMI and I use it for my whole house audio system. My primary is (was - it just got replaced) a 3-5 year old Sony model that is admittedly in a lower class than this Yamaha receiver (the secondary was in a higher class in its time, I think).

While I usually have all Sony stuff, I was completely willing to try another well-known Japanese brand who specializes in receivers and amps. And - it's just awesome. Totally. Not a single regret about the switch. The RX-A880 gave me back everything I lost going from my older, higher-end Sony to my newer one, AND it gave me so many nice surprises on the way! As anyone can tell you that it sounds good and looks good, I'll concentrate on this little details that I discovered during setup:

1) Besides the seven HDMI inputs, it also has a composite video, a component video, two optical audio, one extra (second belongs to component) coax audio, and two composite audio inputs, not to mention phono.

The great thing is that you can assign different audio inputs to any of the video inputs. So, for example, I decided to keep my Wii around since I now have a component input (and it takes up almost no space), but the cable is component video with composite audio, but the component video input on this has coax for the audio. Bummer. But no, you can change it. Example number two is I have a computer in my telecom closet hooked up to this with both HDMI and line-out audio. For circumstances too complicated to define here, audio does not output via the HDMI. But because of this feature, I can make the audio appear when I select the HDMI input OR when I just want to listen to the audio directly (with no HDMI output). Perfect.

2) 9 Speaker outputs. First, I'm so happy to have the 2-zone thing back (my secondary receiver has it, but my other, newer Sony did not - it only had A/B speakers that shared an amp). But this one you can actually have 7.1 AND a second zone (although you can't play them at the same time. This is really cool if you want the best of both worlds. I don't know if I can find a place for two more speakers in my setup, but ...it's nice to have the option. Supposedly, this all works automatically. I imagine it could work fine, but I am unable to try it at the moment.

3) 2-zone done better. My older Sony had 2-zone, but the controls were - frankly - atrocious. It was always confusing, even for someone like me who can be a super A/V nerd and memorize anything. The way I use it now is just to keep the remote on Zone-2, and do Zone-1 on the unit itself.

This Yamaha, however, has a simple switch on the remote, and you're either controlling one zone or the other depending on that switch. Simple and effective. You can also control it from the unit, unlike the older Sony.

4) 8 custom presets, all controlled directly from the remote. Another 8 for Zone 2?!

The one complaint I read by a reviewer was that you have to scroll through all the inputs from the remote to get to what you want. But that doesn't matter for two reasons: first, you can change the settings to skip anything you don't want. But, second, with 8 custom presets - and each with their own remote button - you probably don't even ever need to scroll through the inputs anyway.

And the custom presets are great. You can turn on and off a bunch of features like whether or not it changes your HDMI out settings, if it uses your YPAO settings, extra bass, which speakers it uses, etc. And it even can link the second zone!

Two great examples:

I can't stand to watch regular background TV with the surround sound on because it makes the commercials that much more obnoxious. But of course I like big booming bass and surround for movies. And it's also annoying to switch the unit off and on all the time, especially if you want to use control for HDMI. So I have one preset for very flat TV sound using just the front speakers that is clearer than-, but no more annoying than-, my regular TV speakers. Then I have another preset for surround sound and big bass for movie watching.

I have one preset for straight music just in zone 1. Then I have another preset for straight music in both zones one and two. It turns on zone 2 automatically. I could not figure out how to make a preset just for zone 2, but it seems that when I am controlling zone 2 on the remote, I can make 8 more presets just for zone 2. You can not adjust these presets via menu, from what I can tell, though.

5) 14 character names on the front of the unit in dot matrix. My other receivers were all limited to 8 characters. You can see all 14 at once, which is great.

6) Much more robust networking. I haven't played with this too awful much yet, but it seems that if you start listening to a playlist or an album on your NAS, then the next time you go back to "server", it will start playing where you left off (well, the song you left off at will start over again, instead of at the exact moment you left at), but at least this way you don't have to turn the TV on just to play some music. I suppose you could create a playlist of all Death Metal, and then you just have a stream going whenever you want it. It also seems like you can actually sign into Pandora and all the other stations and listen to your own account. And all the Internet/Network stuff is a separate scroll-through than the other inputs. I really like how that is set up.

6) The "program up/down" buttons on the remote can be programmed to do about 10 different things. I picked to have the dialogue increased or decreased for when you can't hear what people are saying even though everything else is loud enough. To be clear, I think this depends on if the dialogue is known to the decoder. I haven't tried all the other options yet.

7) Remote is awesome. Besides what I mentioned above, you can also make some changes to the red/green/yellow/blue buttons, but I wish you could really program those completely to your liking. Everything is laid out nicely, and the second zone even makes sense, as I mentioned above.

8) I realize the second HDMI output would be great if you also have a projector or something like that. With it, you can have access to all your devices without having to rewire anything. Haven't used it yet, but am glad to have the extra functionality.

...

There's plenty more, but I'm forgetting some of the details right now. I've only played with this thing for a few days, but I like it more and more. The one thing that is missing is that you can't change all the options via the webpage. text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal) I have never had an e-reader before. I used to read a TON, but then I grew up and life happened, so wanted to get back in to it.

I purchased both the Paperwhite and the Oasis. The Paperwhite seemed like a great device, but I could tell immediately how much more my eyes liked the larger screen on the Oasis along with the warmth feature. The warmth feature was the biggest factor for me, as it made it look much more like an actual page out of a book. I've included a picture of the Paperwhite (on the right) and Oasis (left), both set at the same brightness, but with the Oasis's warmth setting on. You can also see there is no white Kindle logo on the Oasis, which I found ever so slightly distracting on the Paperwhite. The quality of the screen on the Oasis is also much better than the Paperwhite - text is more clear and crisp. If you commute a lot or size is important to you, Paperwhite is definitely the way to go.

I was really overwhelmed with the Oasis at first, just because it was so new to me. I'm pretty good with new tech, but the whole environment was slightly overwhelming because it's not just as simple as getting a new device on a platform you're already used to (ie, Windows, Android, Apple, etc). Once I got past the learning curve, I started to actually like it a bit. However, the way the Kindle sorts and handles your books could be much better. You can organize things in to 'Collections', but it still doesn't feel like enough. I recommend looking up Calibre and going from there.

My biggest gripe is the ergonomics of the Oasis. Although it's not much heavier than the Paperwhite, it feels like it because of the shape of it. It just feels heavier because of the weight distribution towards the center, and is awkward to hold with that bump/excessive weight distribution that sticks out. I am a 5'9" woman with 'normal' sized hands, so I can't even imagine how this would be for someone with smaller hands. I bought a case immediately because the shell is ridiculously slippery, and in my opinion, a horrible choice of material for something you're going to hold for hours. Looks pretty, but not very functional for an e-reader. I bought the 'Ayotu Skin Touch Feeling Case', and it is awesome. I ordered a couple of others and this one stood out among all of them big time.

Last gripe is that the screen is pretty slow and laggy at times. I know it's an e-reader, but it's a very expensive one that doesn't do anything else (which to clarify I am absolutely fine with BUT, see next point), but at that price, it should really be perfect.

A positive feature of this that is nice is that you can flip the device around and the screen flips with you, so if you are right or left handed or just want to switch sides during reading, that is super helpful.

I do like it, but am considering whether or not I am going to keep it due to the ergonomics alone.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal)

I can understand the concern because while we have our unit has its own meter, we just never know what may be inadvertently shared, but we (as in me) said, "We have to try it out," and so we finally got the "TP-Link TL-PA7020 KIT_V2 AV1000 2-Port Gigabit Powerline Adapter" up and running last week. It was easy to install. I'm won over because I definitely like not having network cable running across the floor to my room. I honestly don't see much difference in speed which might be a compliment in a way. There is still a lingering concern of someone finding a way to share the link but I really like the convenience so we'll continue to monitor.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Backpack for SLR Cameras and Accessories-Black I was really surprised at the quality of this camera bag given the price. I was looking for a small-ish bag that I could use while hiking and this seemed to be a decent choice, especially since I've been pretty happy with other Amazon Basic products.

The build quality is excellent, with strong seams and zippers that work well. The fabric is more than durable enough to withstand a good amount of abuse. The internal padding is nicely done, and I'm especially pleased with the padding on the straps - very comfortable to wear this for an extended amount of time.

The storage space is more than ample. This usually gets used with my smaller SLRs, but I can fit my Canon 5D Mark II and a few prime lens into this without difficulty. Lots of cubbies to hold all the sundries (cables, battery packs, filters, etc.).

It's not perfect, especially with regard to the tripod straps. I would like those to have been more robust for carrying a heavy tripod. But, for the price, I won't deduct any points for that.

I have bags that cost far more than this, but don't perform any better. Highly recommend, and a great value.

Travel Adapter, 2400W International All in One Universal Travel Power Plug Adapter, Travel Charger with 1 Type-C / 3 USB Port Adapter Plug, Perfect Adapter for UK, EU, AU, US, Over 170 Countries I have two other adapters very similar to this, but there are a few differences.

Like the other two, this is a little larger than initially expected, but it has to be to have all the built-in adapters. There is still no Italy plug or ground conductor, so this is only ideal if you only have an ungrounded device like a computer (again, without ground) and a few USB-chargeable devices like phones and cameras.

This one has a USB-C port, unlike one of my others, but - unlike the one I have that does have USB-C - the total current is more limited. Both adapters with USB-C ports only support 5v output, so they may not charge your device if your device can only accept higher voltage (USB-C has multiple layers of standards, so can be a bit confusing).

I like this adapter when traveling to multiple regions within one trip. Otherwise, I'll just use the cheap adapters which by themselves are smaller. Out of the three I own, I'm not sure which is best; I think it depends on your personal situation. Hopefully I shared enough to help you decide.

TrackR Bravo - Generation 2, Rose Gold (Discontinued by Manufacturer, Generation 3 Now Available) This sounds like it might be a useful gadget, but I could not get it to work. I have a Samsung S6 Android phone. I downloaded the app and created an account. The app says it has discovered the TrackR (via Bluetooth) and shows me a map of its "last seen" location, which I assume is the current location of my phone, not necessarily the location of the TrackR. Unfortunately, that is as far as it works. After that, the app cycles between "discovered, attempting to connect" and "searching" but never seems to succeed. The button on the app does not ring the TrackR device and the button on the TrackR does not ring my phone. I tried contacting TrackR support, but they just responded with a form letter saying due to overwhelming demand, they are not able to respond.

If they do respond and help me get this thing working, I will update this review. Until then, they get 1 star.

Since the entire purpose of the device is being able to locate a lost phone or other valuables in an emergency, malfunctions like this really make it too unreliable to use in real life.
text_fidelity_b: TrackR Bravo - Generation 2, Rose Gold (Discontinued by Manufacturer, Generation 3 Now Available)

Cat8 Ethernet Cable 50FT, JEVIT Internet Network Cord, 40Gbps 2000Mhz LAN Wires, High Speed S/FTP LAN Cables with Gold Plated RJ45 Connector for Router, Modem, Gaming (15m/ 50FT） Keep in mind that since this has a PVC jacket, and since PVC produces toxic smoke, this shouldn't be run from room to room (per code) despite its long length.

Also keep in mind that cat8 doesn't do anything above cat6 unless you have a 10 or 40Gb/s NIC/SFP at both ends of your link, and the total link length is shorter than it was with cat6.

So unless you need a strong backbone link in a data center, don't think you need this.

If you are running a data center, you may want to look elsewhere: this cable appears to be hand wrapped. The connectors were pushed into the body of the roll in a way where the bend radius was dangerously close to being exceeded. I guess there's something to be said for buying the best if you're really using this for business.

Just know what you need and what you're going to do with it. For almost all home applications running from room to room, I'd take a cat6 cable with a legitimate riser or plenum rating any day.
text_fidelity_b: Cat8 Ethernet Cable 50FT, JEVIT Internet Network Cord, 40Gbps 2000Mhz LAN Wires, High Speed S/FTP LAN Cables with Gold Plated RJ45 Connector for Router, Modem, Gaming (15m/ 50FT）

Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 It takes some getting used to. I have three of these Anker ergos. Two are wireless and are in use at work. One is wired and on my gaming rig at home.

Gaming: My normal mouse is a Logitech gaming mouse which had been my go to for many years. It was fast accurate and had plenty of built in controls for everything I needed. This mouse also has all of the relevant controls and the resolution button is less likely to get accidentally hit than on the Logitech. It does still get hit here and there though. I also find that the vertical style while more comfortable is not as ideal for gaming but honestly speaking is a small niggle in that the comfort is far more appreciated than the slightly awkward hand position (as movements need to be very fast). Is this up to par with other premium gaming controllers? I have my doubts, but it is certainly comfortable and as a wired controller is adequate for sure.

Everyday: Just yes. Especially considering the value. It is both affordable as an ergonomic mouse and comfortable. You may need to make adjustments to your seating angle as the tendency is for this mouse to be most comfortable when your forearm is almost flat on the desk surface.

Look and feel: It is not an especially heavy mouse. But it does have a level of refinement expected on something more costly. It is also well designed and not obscenely gaudy like a lot of products these days. The rubbery matte surface is pleasant and tactile and the buttons are responsive and easy to actuate. The mouse is somewhat full-sized. I don't want to say large because I have small-medium hands and I can use this just fine, but by no means do I have small hands. Those who have small hands might find this more of a challenge to use though I don't doubt you'll get used to it. The primary buttons and grip would be fine, but the locations of the scroll wheel and the forward nav button are a bit of a reach.

Like I said I have three of these in various formats and love them all. Other than my ultra compact travel mouse, these are used on all of my home and work devices. At such a reasonable cost you can't lose by at least trying it.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

This is NOT the speaker that you simply grab and throw in the bag and go. This speaker is rather large and surprisingly VERY heavy.

The sound quality is nice but the bass is only ok in my opinion. I have another speaker which is made by Amazon that cost about $50 that has the exact same sound quality. It is loud but as with this bass, ive heard others that are louder and cost much less.

I will start with the app that the instructions tell you that you need to download. It states that it is for updates, but all I saw is that it is used for is linking multiple speakers together.

I wanted this speaker because we spend alot of time out by the pool and at the river during the summer. I knew that I wanted something that was water proof for both of those settings so I was happy to give this one a try. As I mentioned before, this sucker is HEAVY so while it may be water proof, if you were to drop in the river at any point it would go straight to the bottom never to be seen again, so it wouldn't really matter how water proof it is. For the pool and sitting stationary, it would be perfect.

One use that I can see us using this speaker would be for travel baseball games. It is loud enough that you would be able to hear it from a distance.

As I said earlier... some will love this speaker and think that it is absolutely worth it. Others will not. This speaker will strictly come down to personal opinion. For instance, other than the weight, I love this speaker. My spouse thinks that his $50 is much better.

Luby Portable Movie Projector with Free Projector Screen Perfect for Fun Camping Neighborhood Gathering Backyard Movie The listing says this projector supports 1920 X 1080p resolution. It doesn't say it projects in that resolution. And it doesn't. You can see the pixel grid on the home screen. It's definitely not a 1080p projector. I don't even think it's 720p. Text is pretty blurry when you connect it to a computer as a monitor. If you do that, you might want to enlarge the font for readability.

Brightness is pretty good. It's better than mini projectors I've seen in the past. But the room (or outdoors, if you're using it there) will need to be pretty dark to get a good view. The farther away the projector is from the screen, the bigger the picture, the more spread out the light is, the darker the room will need to be to see it.

I had hopes the OS would play DVDs directly from a USB-powered outboard DVD player, but it doesn't have that functionality. I tried it and it would not recognize the connected device. You do have to manually select the input from the home screen. There are multiple inputs: HDMI, VGA, micro SD card, and USB.

The included screen is okay, but a white wall (or even ceiling) works well too.

On the bottom of the projector is a tripod mounting hole, a nice addition.

The manual keystone adjustment works only for up and down adjustment, not side to side. The focus is also manual, and works well.

The two negatives to me are that the remote control pretty much has to be aimed directly at the IR receiver ports on the projector to get it to work (there are ports on the front and back), and there is some trash inside the lens that shows up in the projected image in the one I received. I'll have to open up the projector to blow that out.

Other than that, at this price point, it's a good projector, and pretty versatile in terms of portability and input options.
text_fidelity_b: Luby Portable Movie Projector with Free Projector Screen Perfect for Fun Camping Neighborhood Gathering Backyard Movie

RUBAN Notebook Lock and Security Cable (PC/Laptop) Two Keys 6.6 Foot (Black) This notebook lock and security cable works with laptops that have a Kensington security slot (about 99% of them on the market do), so it will work for most notebooks except the MacBook Pro. Be sure to check to make sure your laptop has the security port which looks like a small slot usually found in the upper right outside corner.

To use this cable run the end of the cable around a fixed object that can't be moved without effort or drawing attention, such as the leg of a heavy table or a post, then loop the locking end through the loop and attach it to your laptop. The locking mechanism has a built in bar that fits into the Kensington slot, so just insert it into the port, then turn the key 90 degrees to lock it in place. You'll need the key to unlock it when you're ready to take the laptop so be sure to bring it along. When you want to remove your laptop just rotate the key in the opposite direction to unlock it. This set comes with a spare key as well in case you misplace one.

The cable that comes with this is 6.2" long which wasn't long enough to go over the top of my desk and come back up to secure my laptop to the desk that way, but it was adequate to secure it around one of the desk's legs, so this cable isn't intended to permanently affix your laptop to a desk top, and it's thin enough to cut with bold cutters, but it's long enough and strong enough to deter someone from being able to snatch and run off with your laptop when you're at the library or coffee shop and want to leave it unattended long enough to go use the copy machine or go get a refill!

I like how the T-bar mechanism works to secure the lock to the laptop but still allow complete cable movement and rotation without dislodging the lock from the laptop, and I also like the fact that the cable is coated to prevent damage to your laptop & whatever the cable is secured around. This laptop lock and security cable is going to be perfect for my daughter when she studies in the campus library.

I received this notebook lock and security cable for testing and review. It works a lot easier than I expected!
