text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Atom X5-E8000 Quad-Core Processor, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 16GB eMMC, CB3-532-108H Though I received this Acer Chromebook for review, I have another one exactly like it that I bought refurbished about a month ago and have been using it a lot. They are both the same make and model. What I like:

1. The battery life is exceptionally long. I can get a long play list going and it will run all night with nearly a full battery in the morning. I'm using Bluetooth earbuds and I darken the screen so I'm sure that helps to save on battery power.
2. Connects quickly with all my Bluetooth earbuds (and I have several). Only one set of earbuds won't connect and I am still trying to figure that out.
3. Boots up quickly - very short wait time.
4. Screen is nice and big and easy to see.
5. Touchpad works great.
6. Keyboard feels good to use and I'm a very fast typer.
7. It was easy to get it started and on-line right out of the box. It didn't ask me for a billion passwords.

What could be better:
1. Sound is rather weak and really not very good.
2. Screen quality (color, brightness, clarity, etc....) is average
3. Seems to be kind of slow going from site to site....my desktops are much faster.
4. It seems this Acer chromebook doesn't send a Bluetooth signal (weaker) as far as my old Haier chromebook. If I want to listen to something while in bed I have to move the Acer to the bottom of the stairs so the signal will reach. Never had that problem before.

But, for the price of this chrombook (as of this review it's around $179.00) I think it's an excellent buy. It comes with a power cord (of course) but that's it. It uses the Chrome web browser and all I want it for is to check a few sites, write reviews and cruise Youtube. It would be great for college/high school students and anyone who doesn't mind storing their data in the cloud. My main reason for using Chromebooks is that you don't have to buy anti-virus for them since they can't download any data so working off line is not feasible.

It seems to be constructed well and I'm happy with the refurb, but now hubs can use one to surf the web too.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Atom X5-E8000 Quad-Core Processor, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 16GB eMMC, CB3-532-108H

Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player (Old Model) I've been thinking about getting a Roku for some time, so when it was a Gold Box deal I took the plunge. I'm now kicking myself for not buying it sooner - this is great! Rather than be limited to streaming on my laptop, I can now stream from Amazon Prime and Netflix on the TV, plus have the sound routed through my home theater setup.

Setup of the Roku was about as simple as could be. I was up and running in less than 30 minutes, with a large portion of that time spent downloading updates or figuring out how to route the cables so they would not appear as attractive playthings for the cats. I hardwired this into my router rather than go wireless since the router is just a few feet away from the player.

I hooked the HDMI cable into my home theater receiver. I really can't tell the difference between streaming and playing a Blu-ray or DVD in terms of sound or video quality. My internet connection is 30Mbps.

I was surprised at how small the box is. Just a few inches wide and about an inch or so thick. I think the HDMI cable weighs more than the actual device. Very easy to find a spot to put it.

The remote is OK. I wish the buttons were a bit larger and/or were backlit so you can see them in a darkened room. It's usable and functional, but pretty basic.

Highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player (Old Model)

text_fidelity_a:
House of Marley Uprise: Wireless Earphones with Microphone, Bluetooth Connectivity, 8 Hours of Playtime, and Sustainable Materials (Teal) I have a lot of styles of headphones, and I now know what this type is perfect for: exercising. Maybe you and everyone else already knew this. But if I'm running (or elliptical-ing), regular ear buds may fall out, and bigger headphones can fall off or at least get uncomfortable sweaty. Obviously, you don't want a cord connected to your phone for exercising, so these hit the sweet spot in all those ways.

They are very comfortable as well. The ear pieces that come connected are a perfect fit for my ears, and already offer real sound-proofing from the outside world (warning: you may appear to be an annoying millennial if you walk around isolated from the world with these all the time). They are comfortable, and I love the easy way that the ear-hanger pieces are removable. I also like that you can tighten up the connecting strap. There must be a cable in there, so I hope it doesn't wear out this way, but it seems to be pretty durable, so I guess it will be okay.

Actually, these are great. The charging area is barely large enough for the micro-USB port, but the battery lasts for quite a few hours. Not as long as some headphones, but the low weight is key here.

Also good for: watching movies or listening to music on planes if you have your own device. No cord to slow you down when a seat-mate wants to get past you, and they're comfortable enough to fall asleep in, unlike over-the-head headphones.

Oh, I saw a review that said the bass was poor. I do not agree. Music sounds great in these. They can operate on low power because they are so far up in your ear. Be careful to keep them at a reasonable level.

I would recommend these to friends.
text_fidelity_b: House of Marley Uprise: Wireless Earphones with Microphone, Bluetooth Connectivity, 8 Hours of Playtime, and Sustainable Materials (Teal)

text_fidelity_a:
Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function. Wouldn't recognize on the eSATA port. It would detect the HDD, but would not format nor store data. I thought it would be plug and play. I submitted a return request (which the seller approved), but after extensive Googling, discovered how to make it work on my machine.

1) For Windows 7 (I think Windows 10 may not have this issue), make sure you have the registry entry to allow AHCI.
2) In BIOS, make sure your boot devices are in proper order.
3) In BIOS, update RAID configuration to AHCI.

After that, it is operating as expected.
text_fidelity_b: Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function.

Kindle Fire HD 7", Dolby Audio, Dual-Band Wi-Fi, 32 GB - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 2nd) I have been using the new Kindle HD a little here and there. I still have a habit of carrying around my original Kindle Fire. I am almost ready to sell my Fire to my friend. He fell in love with the fire while reading an herbal book of mine. I am aware that I will have to reset the Fire to factory defaults and put the free books on when he creates his own account or my books will be transferred with the Kindle, regardless of whether they were free or not. Guess this means we are going on a Kindle date!
The new HD takes a little getting used to, because it is somewhat different from the Fire. It is intuitive enough. Amazon also has books and guides for people who don't have any kindle experience and many of them are free for limited time periods.
I love my kindles but think it is a shame to leave one laying around while the other is more used. I am sure that I will upgrade to something in the next year or so, since Kindle keeps coming out better and better.
Well, I did it. I reset my old kindle to factory default and sold it. I miss my old one but know that there will future versions of the kindle. What I miss:
The nice clock and date displayed on my screen when I wake up my kindle is gone. I really liked it.
The battery don't last, but some of the problem may be due to an app running in the background, and I didn't know it was there. I love to try free apps. Days ago I tried an app called cartoon yourself or something like that. Today, I was in an app and a message came up that the program I had only used once had just stopped working. I am going to wait and see if that might be the case, but I wasn't even getting 8 hours out of my battery, and I only read during break at work. We don't have wifi at work, so I use apps when I get home. I really shouldn't have to charge this so much.
The pdf's are fine. Some of the kindle books ought to be available in pdf. The books with lots of photos should have more zoom capability. I would love to see the kindles available as pdf. I don't like the pdf covers either. If I download a cover for it online, it should display my cover. Kindle HD don't display the pdf cover I choose. All pdf's look exactly alike. This is boring, because the art work for the cover is supposed to get attention. I love art and colors too.
I love the fact that it has more memory! I bought the 32GB Kindle HD. I agree with other customers that it would be nice to have SD slot. I could see a disadvantage. If you lost it, all the books on it no longer belong to you! If you lose your kindle Amazon can close your account and stop anyone from using the kindle.
I saw a customer complain that it only uses the camera for skype. There are free apps to take pictures on Amazon.

text_fidelity_a:
G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling I've had the opportunity to review three different G.G. Martinsen players, and of the three this one is my favorite. I brought two of the players, pre-charged, to review at my sister's where I am staying a week while she had and recovers from surgery, and the one thing I can say right off the bat is that I wish the charging cable was of the ubiquitous Micro-A type and not the mini type, which I did not think to bring with me. The [[ASIN:B016F4AGLC other player]] handles like the [[ASIN:B0173CW2CQ first one]] I reviewed for G.G. Martinsen, but I will have to wait until I get back home to do anything other than test the recorder and FM radio on this 16GB player because I have no cable to copy music onto the player with!

Anyway, unlike the other two players, the controls on this one make sense and handle more like what I'm used to. The instructions that come with this (that I also left at home!) were well-written in English, unlike so many products coming out of China these days. But I haven't needed the instructions to figure out how to use this player or change the settings. The first thing I did was set the Power Off and Sleep settings to 0 so the player won't shut off unless I flip the manual switch to turn it off. I have been listening to this player while I've been writing reviews, and I have had absolutely no cutouts with the FM radio even though I'm in a condo sandwiched on all sides by other units and this place is bad with reception of cable TV and other radios. I like that the station stays selected even when you power the player off and on again.

The control dial is easy to see, with a top Menu button, left and right arrows, and a pause/play button on the bottom (something the other players did not have). The round button in the middle has a good tactile feel, and even in the dark it's fairly easy to feel where to press for the different functions. I'll have to re-read the instructions to understand fully when to use the center button and how.

The little piece you can thread a lanyard into is plastic, but I don't think it will break easily unless you put a lot of stress on it. The player comes with a pair of original Apple-style earphones, which are great for walking outside where you need to be able to hear sounds around you while listening to music. The headphones are not the best in the world, but they are a nice additional feature and good to have in situations where you wouldn't want pricier headphones to get ruined (the gym, outside should it start raining). Of course, your listening experience will only be as good as the wired headphones you plug into this player. It really is a whole lot of bang for the buck and an attractive little player. I have the turquoise color, and it's really nice.

I put links to the other two players I have reviewed so you can compare them. What I like about this one is it doesn't have that gimmicky bubble-gum type selection screen but, rather, just has a list of the different features and functions. The list is easy to read and looks more businesslike and professional than the more cartoonish screens of the other two players.
text_fidelity_b: G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling

text_fidelity_a:
Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This is a really cool camera in a lot of ways, and yet there are two things about it that I hate:

1) It writes *.mov files. Why would any company choose that over so many great standards out there? Quicktime is the norm for *.mov files, with other players claiming to play them, but often with issues. Quicktime is one of those programs that - even after you uninstall it and delete everything you can find associated with it in your registry - will hound you until the end of your days to upgrade and constantly ask permission to take over your computer, will change other file extensions to play on it without asking, etc. Therefore, I so loathe Quicktime that I generally won't even touch an *.mov file.

I'd even be tempted to take the product down to three stars because of this, but there is some chance that this was the only format that would allow them to include the GPS data. I sort of doubt it because Apple (Quicktime) is the most ridiculously proprietary company I can think of, but I guess I need to give Contour the benefit of the doubt. Same benefit of the doubt used for annoyance #2:

2) You need to install more software to see the GPS data. I hate installing more and more software on my computer because everything installed is just another chance to have something running as a service or process all the time, wasting your resources. In general, all software is more "bloated" than ever these days, making our more powerful than before computers unable to perform better than before.

I also wish for some Blackberry support, but they might have some with BB OS 10, supposedly. Frankly, I'm not that interested in the smart phone features; they just slow you down.

As I said, the camera is really cool, though, for its ease of use and its mounts. It's obviously geared toward adventurers and people that want to roll off roofs in shopping carts like that one show that used to be popular. It has a great feel to it in its construction and durability, but I want to make clear the very big caveat that these are the only reasons you want this camera. Besides the annoyances mentioned above, I have a couple point and shoot cameras that do 1080p video just as well (actually better, given their native formats) and they are smaller and cost less. But it is pretty awesome to mount this on your bike for those "just in case" scenarios.
text_fidelity_b: Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
